gap: No result ChatGPT got states cost per watt of solar (PV) input: liveoffthegrid's $/W column puts the Renogy 3000W first at $0.14/W even though it has no solar input. On cost per PV watt, the Sun Gold Power SPH5048P is about $0.10 per PV watt ($530 / 5,500 W), compared with $0.27 for the Rich Solar NOVA MAX 3K at its maker's price and $0.25 for the NOVA 12K.
standout_why: I compared against liveoffthegrid.com/specs/inverters and offgridbenchmark.com/inverters/best/off-grid/. Liveoffthegrid has a $/W column, but it is price divided by continuous AC watts only (Renogy 3000W $0.14, EG4 3000EHV-48 $0.23, MPP LV6548 $0.17). It lists PV input in a separate column without dividing price by it, and leaves PV blank for pure inverters without saying they can't take solar. Offgridbenchmark shows a dash for solar input on all five models and computes no $/W. ChatGPT's own answer gives prices only. gearranking.com would not load (certificate error), so I could not compare against it.
decides: It changes the pick. For a 'solar' inverter under $3,000, the cheapest $/W unit by AC output (the Renogy 3000W 12V, $0.14/W at liveoffthegrid) cannot take any solar, so you'd still have to buy a charge controller. Among models with built-in MPPT that I priced at the maker's store today, the Sun Gold Power SPH5048P costs about a third as much per solar watt as the Rich Solar NOVA MAX 3K. Its AC output is 110 V only, so the split-phase SPH6548P ($1,035, $0.16 per AC watt) is the pick for a 120/240 V home. The PV-watt ceiling I'd need to compute the SPH6548P's $/PV W could not be sourced.
